source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. The original algorithm provenance was checked against the catalog record for Treiber's IBM RJ 5118 report; linearizability/progress against Herlihy-Wing and Herlihy; reclamation against Michael, Brown, Crossbeam, and Harris; and current atomic contracts against the C++ draft, Java 21 AtomicReference, and Rust atomic documentation. Seven sources resolved directly. ACM publisher pages denied automated retrieval and IEEE DOI returned accepted metadata; their use is limited to bibliographic and scoped theorem attribution. The obsolete IBM PDF host was not used as evidence.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines atomic head H, null, node fields, Reach(H), node lifecycle states, push/pop CAS proposals, attempt/failure/commit counts, and ABA/tag generations.
The chapter distinguishes logical reachability, local pointer observation, protection, retirement, reclamation, value ownership, and storage reuse.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Reviewed list order, finite/acyclic predicates, equality versus identity, atomic event notation, set/state overlaps, and progress-scope qualifications.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-052/report.json records the eight exact events, P2=B/P1=C pops, final stack A, six CAS attempts, one failure, five commits, and all A/B/C values accounted once.
Independent replay confirms two initial push commits, P2 pop, C push, one failed P1 proposal, one refreshed P1 pop, and unchanged C/A state across failure.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts are for a stipulated abstract history with stable identities and do not measure concurrent retry or prove lock-free progress.

evidence: A successful push CAS adds one initialized private node before the prior valid list; a successful pop CAS removes exactly the valid first node; a validated null observation implements empty pop.
Ordering successful CAS/null linearization events maps every completed history to sequential LIFO while failed CAS events make no abstract transition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof is conditional on well-defined protected reads, immutable published links, target atomic semantics, publication ordering, and safe reclamation.

evidence: Reviewed empty, one-node, last-node, simultaneous push/pop, stale next, spurious failure, address reuse, generation wrap, unprotected reader, delayed hazard/epoch participant, allocator failure, and destructor re-entry.

Reviewed cancellation before/after CAS, close-admission races, bounded-capacity reservation, quiescent shutdown, target atomic fallback, GC pauses, contention/starvation, process crash, and safety-critical use.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans abstract LIFO, memory order, pointer lifetime, identity, progress, space, lifecycle, target portability, operational performance, and deployment.

evidence: Reach(H) remains one finite acyclic chain of uniquely reachable initialized nodes with immutable next; private publication and successful removal transfer node/value ownership exactly once.

Every dereference follows protection and validation; every removed node retires once and reclaims after stale observations are impossible; shutdown prevents entry and waits for observers/retired cleanup.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across allocate, initialize, observe, protect, validate, publish, retry, remove, retire, reclaim, cancel, close, drain, destroy, and quiesce.

evidence: The representation-preservation and linearization argument covers successful push, successful pop, empty pop, and failed CAS separately.

The lock-free kernel argument charges mismatch failures to competing successful head commits and explicitly excludes unbounded spurious failure, allocation, blocking reclamation, target fallback, and wait-free individual completion.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides a scoped paper proof, not machine-checked source refinement, weak-memory proof, reclaimer proof, infinite-state liveness proof, or deployed implementation certification.

evidence: Linearizability, lifetime safety, ABA resistance, lock-free logical progress, bounded memory, fairness, shutdown, and performance are explicitly separate claims.
Hazards, epochs, tags, reference counts, GC, never-reclaim, elimination, arrays, and mutexes are presented with their assumptions and unresolved obligations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Exact abstract transitions, conditional proof obligations, implementation strategies, empirical comparisons, real-time requirements, and human safety review remain distinguishable.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-052 passed the deterministic stale-CAS history with recorded interpreter version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit code zero.

The chapter requires history checking, controlled reuse/wrap, delayed readers, sanitizers, bounded model checking, weak-memory analysis, target atomic verification, and stress metrics for attempts, starvation, cache traffic, reclamation, and retained memory.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential list model proves no threads, atomicity, memory ordering, pointer lifetime, ABA prevention, reclamation, linearizability of source code, lock-freedom, scalability, or deployment safety.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed abstract LIFO/representation, push, protected pop, linearization, progress, ABA, reclamation, ordering, ownership/destruction, boundedness, close/shutdown, contention/alternatives, cancellation/failure, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed private allocation before retry, release/acquire publication, protection-before-dereference and revalidation, stable identities/generations, exact retire ownership, allocator/reclaimer/target qualification, cancellation commitment, close admission, operation registry, quiescent cleanup, target stress, raw histories, and mature-library preference.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds lifetime beyond the head CAS; exposition progresses from LIFO proof through target lifecycle; the stale-proposal trace is reproducible; ten worked examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from linearizability to railway-safety transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external concurrency-theory, formal-methods, C++/Java/Rust, compiler, architecture, memory-reclamation, real-time, surgical, railway, regulatory, operational, or safety review is claimed. The model establishes neither source implementation safety nor linearizability, ABA resistance, reclamation correctness, lock-free progress, bounded memory/time, scalability, or deployment safety.
